plain: Guided by careful, practical good sense

webster.text: Proceeding from prudence; dictated or prescribed by prudence; as prudential motives; prudential rules.

example.quote: The greater danger of error, as far as it is supposable, may be a prudential reason for caution in practice, but it cannot be a rule of restrictive interpretation.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, Opinion as to the Constitutionality of the Bank of the United States, Feb. 23, 1791
